definition: Overview of nuclear power generation and its tradeoffs.
core_idea: Nuclear plants use fission to convert water into steam; nuclear fuel is extremely energy-dense (a pound of highly enriched uranium is roughly equivalent to a million gallons of gasoline), but enriched uranium faces supply shortages, environmental concerns, and difficult, unsafe long-term storage once discarded.
key_points: Nuclear generators use nuclear fission to turn water into steam, similar in principle to fossil fuel plants
Nuclear fuel has very high energy density per unit weight (1 lb enriched uranium ≈ 1 million gallons of gasoline)
Enriched uranium supply is subject to severe shortages
Nuclear fuel presents environmental problems and is difficult to store safely once discarded
relationships: Power generation technologies: fossil fuel plants
